records.title: A dump's missing page numbers are not always lost text
records.summary: Quranpedia's al-Sa'di dump has no piece for 42 page numbers, which the first build read as 42 lost pages; walking every passage against Shamela's copy of the same edition showed most of those pages sit inside the piece before, and the real losses are seven passages whose piece breaks off, which the build now fills from Shamela.
records.problem: The al-Sa'di build marked '[…]' wherever the dump's page numbers jumped, so 34 passages showed a gap, and 3:96-97 broke off mid-word. The question was which text was really missing and where to get it.
records.approach: turath.io's export of Shamela book 42 (same al-Risala 2000 edition, page numbers as printed, inline ⦗page⦘ marks) has every page. scripts/quran/sadiShamela.ts finds the last 40 letters before each '[…]' in Shamela (letters only, tashkeel and hamza seats folded, ﷺ and similar signs spelled out), and takes what follows up to the text after the gap or the next range marker. 27 of the 34 gaps filled with nothing; seven filled with real text (3:96-97, 4:11-12, 12:110-111 about 10,000 characters, 18:60-82, 24:11-26, 48:29, 61:10-14). The build then walks every passage against Shamela in 60-letter steps and prints any run it lacks.
records.conditions: Quranpedia tafsir-book-3 dump 2026-08-10; turath book 42 export pinned by sha256 on 2026-11-15.
records.evidence: scripts/quran/sadiShamela.ts, scripts/quran/buildTafsirSadi.ts, shared/quran/tafsirSadiData.test.ts.
records.implication: Before calling text missing from a dump, compare it with a second copy of the same edition letter by letter; page numbering gaps and truncation are different faults. A cut-off piece is the one to look for.
records.text: The audit also catches false alarms from refrains «فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان» matching early; it ignores a jump whose skipped words are in the passage or the one before.

records.title: An off-screen page's sr-only labels widen the whole document
records.summary: Putting the website's three utilities side by side in a scroll-snap row blanked the page in screenshots: the calendar's sr-only day labels are position absolute, so in the off-screen pane they escaped the row's clip and stretched the right-to-left document 650px to the left.
records.problem: A horizontal pager (overflow-x auto, scroll snap) clips its panes, but an absolutely positioned child is clipped only by a scroll container that is also its containing block. The calendar's Tailwind sr-only spans had no positioned ancestor inside the row, so they counted toward the document's width; the right-to-left page grew to 1044px and headless screenshots came out blank.
records.approach: Give each pane position: relative, so every absolute part of a page is held, and clipped, by its own pane.
records.conditions: Chromium (Playwright) at 390px, Next.js page in dir=rtl, panes laid out with flex 0 0 100%.
records.evidence: src/components/utilities/Utilities.module.css (.pane).
records.implication: When a page puts content off screen in a scroll row, make each slide a positioned box. If a screenshot comes out blank, compare document.documentElement.scrollWidth with the viewport before anything else.
records.text: Removing panes one at a time found the calendar as the cause; elementFromPoint still saw the page, which is why the content looked present but never painted where the screenshot looked.

records.title: A rule kept in one branch of a component misses its other paths; a shrink-to-fit label that only iOS shrinks
records.summary: Top-down trees were never meant to have tabs, yet the home pair card drew them, and on the owner's iPhone every tab label was a speck. The no-tab rule lived only in BranchTree's own node branch; the compare tree, added later, went through its nodeContent branch, which drew a tab with no direction check. The speck came from adjustsFontSizeToFit, which the web export the tests run on ignores.
records.problem: #776 (2026-11-14) drew compare cards with the branches tree and put the sides' names on tabs through `nodeContent`. The rule 'a tree drawn top down keeps its reference inside the box' (owner) was coded as `!shared.down` in the default node path only, so the custom path ignored it, on the app and the website. #783 (2026-11-15) then added adjustsFontSizeToFit to the tab label to stop iOS cutting «الأعراف…»; in a tab sized by its own text, iOS shrank every label far below minimumFontScale. Screenshots and e2e run on the web export, where neither the shrink nor the tab's look on a real phone showed.
records.approach: Make the direction rule hold for every node path: the custom path also puts the name inside the box, over a rule, when the tree is drawn top down (app BranchTree, website BranchTree's [data-down] styles). Drop adjustsFontSizeToFit; a label too long is clipped (ellipsizeMode clip), never shrunk or cut to «…». Tests: app home e2e (no node-tab in the pair card, tab text at least 10px), website e2e (a [data-down] name has no top border, normal size), and a source check that no app file uses adjustsFontSizeToFit.
records.conditions: Expo app on iOS (Expo Go), iPhone 17 Pro Max; website and app web export at 440px.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/BranchTree.tsx (NodeTab, custom node path); src/app/quran/branches/BranchTree.tsx; e2e/app/home.spec.ts; e2e/web/pages.spec.ts; src/app/quran/branches/treeTabs.test.ts.
records.implication: When a component has more than one way to draw the same thing (default and custom content, own and render props), put a layout rule where every path passes, and check each path when a rule is added. A text-fitting prop that only native honours needs a real-phone check before merge, or not to be used: the web export cannot show it.
records.text: The same day a third case of the pattern showed: 785 let the surah chips rise into the studio bar's empty room under a tree TreeCard , but the matrix view's chips are drawn by TreePager's footer, so on the home card's matrix they kept the whole bar's room and left a gap under the buttons. Fixed by tucking them there too whenever no studio bar is showing. The owner asked how the pills got there, not only to remove them. Two separate changes met on one card: 776's tabs on compare trees the rule's other path , and 783's shrink-to-fit a native-only prop no test could see . Follow-up owner, 2026-11-16 : one layout for every tree. Tabs are gone; every box, side by side or top down, names its ayah inside over a rule, so there is no second path left to miss. treeTabs.test.ts fails if a tab comes back.

records.title: A grammar book quoting the Quran in its own spelling meets the mushaf by consonants
records.summary: Al-'Ukbari's headings name Quran words in standard spelling, so finding them in the mushaf's Uthmani words worked once both were cut to consonants and searched first among the quoted ayat.
records.problem: The i'rab sheet must show al-'Ukbari's passage under the word it parses. His headings «قوله تعالى: (كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ)» are vocalized standard Arabic; the reader's words are Uthmani rasm with marks the book never uses (open tanwin U+08F0-08F2, dagger alif, small waw), and the book names the ayah only in an earlier «قال تعالى» quote whose number format varies.
records.approach: Compare consonant skeletons: strip vowel marks including U+08D3-08FF, then drop alif, waw, ya and hamza seats, and allow one leading ف, ل, ب or ك to differ. Search the heading in the last quote's ayat (or, when that quote is behind the last ayah found, around that ayah), then three either side, then the next 20 ayat, taking a hit there only when it is unique. Read quote numbers inside and right after the parenthesis, single or double.
records.conditions: Quranpedia e3rab-book-309 version 2026-08-10 against morphology.json 2026-11-14 (corpus Uthmani text). 5,795 passages, 5,616 on words, 179 on whole ayat, 63 line headings merged into the passage before; 14 passages still sit on an ayah well before the one ahead of them, some of them al-'Ukbari's own look back.
records.evidence: scripts/quran/irabUkbari.ts, scripts/quran/irabUkbari.test.ts, shared/quran/irab.test.ts
records.implication: To place a book's Quran quotes on mushaf words, match consonant skeletons within the book's own ayah context before searching wider, and include the Arabic Extended-A mark range when stripping marks.
records.text: The first pass placed 2,964 of 4,737 passages on words. Three things held the rest back. The mushaf text writes tanwin with the open forms in Arabic Extended-A ࣰ ࣱ ࣲ , outside the usual U+064B-065F range, so «مُّحَمَّدࣱ» never met «مُحَمَّدٌ». About a fifth of the quotes put the ayah number after the closing parenthesis, « … ٨٢ .», so the ayah context lagged one quote behind and later headings were searched in the wrong ayah. And much of the book names words inline, «وَ هَلُوعًا : حَالٌ», without «قوله تعالى». Dropping alif, waw and ya from both sides is what makes the rasm and the book's spelling meet «ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ» and «الصَّلَاةَ» both become «صله» . Within one ayah, collisions are rare enough that the first run of matching words is the right one. Tried - Match after stripping only U+064B-065F and U+06D6-06ED → tanwin in Extended-A blocked every word that carried it. - Read quote numbers only inside the parenthesis → passages after « … ٨٢ .» landed on the ayah of the quote before. - Search the whole surah for a unique match → a word spelled with a prefix the match did not forgive «رَءُوفٌ» for «لَرَءُوفࣱ» landed on a later ayah that has it bare 2:143 → 2:207 ; a review found it by listing passages that run back in book order. - Leave unmatched line headings as new passages on the quoted ayah → cross-references to other surahs « الأنعام: ١٥٣ » became passages on al-Baqara; they now stay in the passage before.

records.title: A branch key names where it starts, not what its leaf shows
records.summary: Tree labels printed each branch's ayah key, so a leaf grown into the next ayah or surah showed text under the wrong ayah or surah name.
records.problem: Tree nodes are keyed by the ayah a branch starts in. Branches that grow past their ayah end (identical ayat, run-ons) carry words of the next ayah, sometimes of the next surah, yet the label printed only the key.
records.approach: shownAyat(node, path) in shared/quran/branches.ts names the key and, when the node's words run past an ayah end, the end of the run (ayahEnds); ayatLabel prints «البقرة ٣–٤» or «الصافات ١٨٢ ثم ص ١», matching the ayah cards. Web tree, web quiz answers, app tree, app quiz rows and graded nodes all use it.
records.conditions: trees.json at 2026-11-14; thousands of node labels across the 1,056 trees named only the key while showing words of a later ayah, 3 kinds of surah crossing among them (37:182, 56:96, 69:52 and corpus-follow paths).
records.evidence: shared/quran/treeLabels.test.ts rebuilds every tree and checks each label against the Quran text read from the key to the named ayah (with the basmala before a new surah); src/app/quran/branches/page.test.tsx checks the reported tree.
records.implication: A label for a node must come from the words the node shows, not from the id it is filed under. Check labels against the corpus text, not against the tree's own keys.
records.text: The owner saw «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ص والقرآن ذي الذكر» under «الصافات ١٨٢» on the الحمد لله رب العالمين tree. The tree was right: 37:182 and 1:2 are identical, so both grow into their next ayah until they split. The label was wrong: it printed the key, and the key is where the branch starts. The same was true inside a surah al-Fatiha 2's leaf reads ayah 3 , which is why the data test found thousands of nodes, not one. The test reads the text from the corpus rather than from the tree, so it would also catch a label that names the wrong ayah inside the right surah.

records.title: A reader book has more routes than the dataset
records.summary: Al-Nashr gives some riwayat a second reading from al-Tayyiba routes; checked against the Shatibiyya routes the dataset follows, four 'doubtful' qira'at entries were right and one correction added a reading too many.
records.problem: An audit of the qira'at data against Ibn al-Jazari's al-Nashr flagged entries where the book gives a riwaya two routes and the data names one, and a correction gave Shuba both of his al-Nashr readings of جبريل.
records.approach: Name the route scope first: the twenty riwayat follow al-Shatibiyya and al-Durra. Keep a second reading only when it is on those routes, and confirm with the King Fahd riwaya mushaf where one exists (Shuba prints جَبۡرَئِلَ only; Qunbul ميكائيل and al-Bazzi خطوات match the data).
records.conditions: Quranpedia qira'at dump 2026-11-14 (same output as 2026-11-07); al-Nashr vol. 2 ed. al-Dabba; King Fahd texts for seven riwayat from fawazahmed0/quran-api.
records.evidence: docs/audits/qiraat-source-audit.md; scripts/quran/qiraatCorrections.json; shared/quran/qiraatData.test.ts
records.implication: Before calling a qira'at entry wrong or incomplete from al-Nashr, ask whether the extra reading is a Tayyiba route; the data's scope is Shatibiyya and Durra.
records.text: Al-Nashr collects every route Ibn al-Jazari accepted, so it often says a riwaya reads a word two ways. The dataset, like the King Fahd mushafs, follows one route per riwaya, the one in al-Shatibiyya or al-Durra. An audit that compares the two without naming that scope finds "missing" readings that are not missing. At 2:97 and 2:98 the dump wrongly put Shuba with Ibn Kathir. The first fix gave him both al-Nashr forms, جَبْرَئِيل al-Ulaymi and جَبْرَئِل Yahya ibn Adam . Al-Shatibiyya reads Shuba through Yahya ibn Adam «وَالْيَاءُ يَحْذِفُ شُعْبَةٌ» , and the King Fahd Shuba mushaf prints جَبۡرَئِلَ, so only that one stays. Tried - give Shuba both al-Nashr routes → a second reading the app's riwayat do not have - leave four entries "doubtful" pending a scope decision → the scope was already fixed by the riwayat list

records.title: A tafsir dump keyed by ayah can hold book pages, not the passages that explain the ayah
records.summary: Quranpedia's al-Sa'di dump gives each ayah the page pieces its passage touches, so an ayah's text started with the passage before; the book had to be laid end to end and cut again at its own range markers.
records.problem: The tafsir sheet must show al-Sa'di's passage for the pressed ayah and nothing else. The dump's ayahs[].content looks like that passage, but up to about surah 9 each piece is a whole printed page, later a page cut at passages, and the front matter, appendices, next-surah headings and next-volume title pages hang on neighbouring ayat.
records.approach: Collect every distinct (page, text) piece in page order, clean it (editor footnotes and marks, page markers, next-surah headings), and cut the continuous text at the book's range markers ({١ - ٧} and ﴿١٣، ١٤﴾). A range starting lower than the last, or at 1 with the basmala, opens the next surah. A passage runs to the ayah before the next marker; a marker inside a wider range cuts it there; an ayah split between two passages (2:219) gets both. The build fails unless every ayah of every surah falls in a passage.
records.conditions: tafsir-book-3.json.gz version 2026-08-10, 920 pages, 42 pages missing from the dump (marked [...] where text breaks off).
records.evidence: scripts/quran/buildTafsirSadi.ts, shared/quran/tafsirSadiData.test.ts (2:11, 2:67, 28:35, 2:219, 3:96, 3:128)
records.implication: Before trusting a per-ayah field in a book dump, check whether its text starts and ends where the book's own markers do, on an early and a late surah; dedupe by text and test the first and last lines of passages, not only coverage.
records.text: The handover's converter deduplicated the per-ayah content and treated each group as a passage. Two reviews found what that hid: al-Fatiha carried al-Baqara's heading, 2:11 opened on 2:10's commentary, 28:35 showed all of 28:1-51 under one header, and volume title pages sat after the last passage of each volume. The dump's schema calls the field content, but its unit is the printed page. Reading the book once, in page order, and cutting where al-Sa'di cut is the only grouping that is his. Tried - Dedupe each ayah's pieces and keep the dump's grouping → passages began mid-commentary and ranges were the dump's, not the book's. - Cut at markers but start a new surah when a range repeats → al-Sharh and al-Tin are both «\{١ - ٨\}» and merged; the basmala after the marker is the reliable sign. - Keep each marker's full range → ranges nested \{١ - ٥١\} then \{٣٠ - ٥١\} served two passages under one header.

records.title: Letting go of a shared studio to swap its target closes the studio
records.summary: The app's branches pager re-claimed the growth studio through an effect cleanup, so any change of what the studio plays went through 'no owner' and closed it; a switch inside the studio needs the target swapped in place.
records.problem: The phone app's growth studio is one module-level player that screens claim with claimTarget(owner, target). TreePager claimed it in an effect and released it in that effect's cleanup. A change of owner closes the studio, and a release followed by a claim counts as two owner changes, so every re-run of the effect (a new tree, a connection tag toggled, and now the matrix's read-along/connections switch) closed the studio.
records.approach: TreePager now swaps its target in place: the effect calls claimTarget('branches', next) with no cleanup, a separate unmount effect releases it, and an effect on the open piece closes the studio so a new tree still starts with the studio shut. setTarget stops a running play but keeps the studio open. The website's Grow.tsx registers targets the same release-then-claim way; there setMatrixPlay sets a short-lived `switching` flag that the register and release calls read to keep `studio` open.
records.conditions: Expo app (mobile/src/lib/growPlayer.ts claimTarget) and Next.js site (src/app/quran/branches/Grow.tsx), 2026-11-14, adding the matrix read-along studio with a switch on book matrices.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/TreePager.tsx, src/app/quran/branches/Grow.tsx setMatrixPlay; e2e/app/quran.spec.ts 'every matrix has one studio'
records.implication: When a control inside the studio changes what the studio plays, check that the studio is still open after it: a target swap must not go through a release. A UI test presses the control and then looks for a studio-only button.
records.text: The first build of the switch flipped the matrix from its connections to the read-along and the studio vanished at once. Nothing in the switch closed it: the pager's effect cleanup released the studio, claimTarget saw its owner change from the branches tab to nobody and closed it, then the new claim saw nobody become the branches tab and closed it again. Releasing in the cleanup had been harmless only because every earlier re-run also meant "a different tree", where closing is wanted. Splitting the two meanings swap the target in place; close on a new piece keeps both behaviours. Tried - toggle the switch with the cleanup release in place → studio closed on every switch

records.title: A video that redraws the app from its own constants drifts from the app
records.summary: The tree video drew boxes, lines and labels from numbers copied out of BranchTree, so every later change to the app left the video behind; it now takes each label's and line of words' place from the app's own layout.
records.problem: The phone app records the growing tree on a canvas in a web view (mobile/src/lib/scene.ts), since Expo Go cannot record a native view. The recorder had its own copy of the tree's look: leaf-shaped box corners from before the owner chose round ones, sharp connector corners where BranchTree curves them, a sans-serif 12px label where the app sets Amiri at 12 x 1.12, guessed line and label spacing, fixed places for the chips and card. Each was right once and none followed the app's later changes; the owner saw two different components.
records.approach: BranchTree now registers every label (References, the ruled header) and every Words text with a ref (usePart), and measureScene measures them against the tree root and hands them to the video as each box's parts. The recorder draws each part in its measured rect, so line breaks, spacing and alignment come from the app. What a canvas still has to draw itself takes the app's numbers by name: CARD's radius 14 on every corner, the 14-point stub plus half the 2-point line, the 10-point curve at a fan's ends, Text's 1.12 scale for interface sizes, the matrix card's 12/8 padding and 21/44 ayah lines. Lit lines are drawn after plain ones so grey never covers the path. The frame stacks tree, chips and card as TreeCard does, measured once the fonts load.
records.conditions: Expo app, canvas recorder in a WebView, 2026-11-14. Recording the real native view would need a dev build with a native encoder.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/BranchTree.tsx usePart and measureScene; mobile/src/lib/scene.ts drawText, strokeEdge, layout; e2e/app/quran.spec.ts 'the tree video draws each box from where the app laid out its labels and words'
records.implication: When a video or image redraws an app screen, feed it the app's measured layout rather than copied numbers, and when you change the look of a tree, card or chip, check the video frame beside the app screen.
records.text: The owner put the app's studio beside a video frame and named four gaps: the path, the spacing, the node shapes and the font. All four came from the same cause: the recorder had its own idea of the tree. Tried - matching each constant by hand 753 → right on the day, wrong once the app changed

records.title: A video that redraws a screen drifts from it
records.summary: The compare video drew its own version of the compare card in a canvas, so every later change to the app's card (marks, sizes, the read word, the story parts) left the video behind; it now draws from the same measures and the same layout pieces the app renders.
records.problem: Share-as-video records a canvas inside a web view (the app) or a frame (the website), so it cannot render the app's React Native components. The compare recorder had guessed the card: no card box, labels centred in sans-serif, the ayah number muted, a thick bar under the read word, related marks as a faded root colour, one block of text for story cards and one-to-many cards, the emblem on every frame and a title frame first. The owner found the same drift in the tree video and asked that every video use the app's own nodes.
records.approach: shared/quran/compareCardLook.ts holds the card's measures (COMPARE_CARD, in phone points), the mark colours (markColour), the side names (sideTitle) and the card's layout as pieces (sideView: ayat runs, story-part rules, stretch gaps, picked and unpicked partners, silent parts). The app's CompareCard renders those pieces with those measures, and the recorder draws the same pieces scaled by 1080 / 390, so a change to the card changes the video. Interface text is Amiri at the app's UI_SCALE; a card taller than the frame scrolls with the reading, as on the phone, instead of shrinking the text to nothing.
records.conditions: Expo app (mobile/src/components/CompareCard.tsx, mobile/src/lib/compareVideo.ts) and Next.js site (src/app/quran/compare/CompareVideo.tsx), one recorder in shared/video/compareVideo.ts, 2026-11-14.
records.evidence: shared/quran/compareCardLook.test.ts; frames compared side by side with the app's web export at 390 pt (/mnt/project-files/video-match/).
records.implication: A drawing that copies a screen (a video, an image, a widget) takes its sizes, colours and structure from a module the screen itself uses, never from numbers typed again. Check it by putting a frame next to the screen at the same moment.
records.text: The video's canvas cannot hold React Native views, so "reuse the component" here means reusing everything under the component: the measures, the colour rule and the code that decides what a side shows. Only the last step, turning a piece into pixels, is written twice once as views, once as canvas calls , and it is short. Recording the real screen instead capturing the rendered card per word would reuse the views themselves, but it needs a phone build to test and hundreds of captures per page video; it stays an option if the canvas drifts again. Tried - shrinking the text until a story card fits the frame → at 30 px a long story card still overflowed and the text was too small to read; scrolling with the reading replaced it

records.title: A type import through settings pulled all tree data into the first frame
records.summary: The theme read settings, settings read branchList for one empty value, and branchList loaded trees.json and mutashabih.json, so even a loading screen waited for 12 MB of data.
records.problem: A loading screen cannot show before data loads if anything it imports reaches the data, and the import chain that does it is not visible in the file.
records.approach: Traced the first frame's import graph with an esbuild metafile (entry app/_layout.tsx, packages external, @/screens and AppShell external): theme -> settings -> branchList -> branchInventory -> trees.json. Moved ListState and EMPTY_LIST to lib/listState.ts; the first frame fell from 12 MB to 0.07 MB. Route files other than home wrap their screen (src/screens/) with lib/lazyScreen.ts, because expo-router reads every route file when the navigators mount; launch fell from 23.3 MB to 15.3 MB of source.
records.conditions: Expo 58, expo-router with sync route imports on native, Metro without inline requires (Expo's default). Sizes are source bytes, not device timings.
records.evidence: mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx, mobile/src/lib/lazyScreen.ts, mobile/src/lib/listState.ts
records.implication: Keep app/_layout.tsx, lib/theme.ts, lib/settings.ts and components/LoadingScreen.tsx free of data imports, even for one constant. A new screen goes in src/screens/ with a lazyScreen route file, not straight in app/.
records.text: Metro evaluates a module when it is first required, and an ES import is a require at the top of the module, so one import of a small constant evaluates everything that constant's file imports. settings.ts needed only the empty branches-list value, but branchList.ts also builds the tree inventory, so the theme read by every screen, the loading screen included waited for trees.json, mutashabih.json and branchVerdicts.json. expo-router builds every screen of a navigator when the navigator mounts, which requires every route file, so each route file's imports load at launch whether or not the screen is opened. The route files now only require their screen inside a component; AppShell starts warmScreens after home is drawn so the first visit to a tab is still quick. Home's own data trees, mutashabih, branch verdicts, compare cards, mushaf words still loads at launch; splitting it needs the home feed to change how it picks its first cards. Tried - Metro inlineRequires → Expo turns it off on purpose because it ignores side effects the storage setup import and the splash call depend on order ; not used.

records.title: One-to-many compare cards reuse link ids
records.summary: Finding which compare-card links pair words written differently, across all partners of a one-to-many card at once, coloured an exact pair amber, because every partner numbers its links from the same ids; counting only the partner picked fixed it.
records.problem: The one word rule (docs/adr/0037) finds written pairs on compare cards when they draw (writtenLinks), so the stored cards stay as they are. The first version gathered the exact marks of every partner of a one-to-many card into one map keyed by link.
records.approach: manyCard in src/app/quran/compare/buildCards.ts runs wordMarks on each partner alone, so each partner names its links 0-0, 0-1 and so on, and encodeCard maps those strings to the same numbers card-wide. writtenLinks now takes the picked option and reads only that partner's ayah and shared ayah; the app card, the website card and the video pass the option they show.
records.conditions: compareCards.js as encoded on 2026-11-14.
records.evidence: shared/quran/compareCardLook.test.ts ('written differently' case with a reused link id); shared/quran/compareCardLook.ts writtenLinks.
records.implication: A compare card's link id is unique only within one partner of a one-to-many card. Anything that joins marks across partners has to key by partner too.
records.text: A second review caught it; the first test gave each partner distinct link ids, so it passed.

records.title: Zooming a page with a scale transform enlarges a picture, not the text
records.summary: The mushaf reader zoomed by drawing the page bigger and scaling the view; on iPhone the text came out blurry and cut off at the sides, so zoom became a font size with the words wrapped again and the page scrolled down.
records.problem: Pinch zoom in the app's reader (#664) drew the page at width times zoom inside a view scaled back down, then scaled that view up again. On the owner's iPhone the text was blurry and pixelated, and the lines ran past both edges of the screen, so reading meant dragging sideways.
records.approach: Make zoom a text size. At 1 the printed page stays as it is. Above 1 each word group is measured once at a base size, the page's words are broken into new lines at the screen's width (breakLines in mobile/src/lib/pageZoom.ts), every line except a paragraph's last is spread edge to edge, and the page grows taller inside a vertical scroll view. While the fingers move, a scale transform only previews the new size; when they lift, the page is set again at that size. On the website, the lines become inline text with text-align: justify in flow mode, and a two-finger touch or ctrl+wheel sets the size.
records.conditions: Expo app on iOS with Reanimated transforms on a view of nested Text; Next.js reader on phone browsers. Web-export screenshots don't show the blur: transforms there re-rasterize text sharply.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/ReaderPager.tsx, MushafPageView.tsx (rows), Reader.tsx (scroll, anchor); src/app/quran/read/MushafPage.tsx fit(), Mushaf.module.css [data-flow]
records.implication: Don't zoom text with a transform past the gesture itself: change the font size and lay the text out again. Check anything that measures positions (highlight bands, write boxes, kept scroll) at the new layout, after it is drawn, not in the same render.
records.text: The old zoom kept the page's 15 lines and made everything bigger, which is what a picture viewer does. iOS draws text once into a layer and a scale transform then stretches those pixels, so the letters blurred. The owner asked for the behaviour of a book app instead: bigger words, more lines, scroll down. Flowing lines need each word's width, not each line's, so the page now measures every word group once at the base size; a printed line's width is the sum of its groups and the gaps, the same number as before. The pinch needs an anchor: the share of the page's height that was between the fingers is kept, and once the page reports its new height the scroll puts the same words back under them. The first try used the anchor in the same render as the new size, before the page had reported its new height, and landed at the top. Tried - Anchor applied when zoom changed → used the old height; fixed by waiting until the page reports a different height. - Restoring the saved scroll on the first height report → the first report is the screen's height before words are set , so it clamped to 0; fixed by waiting for a height past the screen's.

records.title: A box hidden by opacity still holds its place, and lines drawn from layout reach it
records.summary: The app's growth studio drew each branch's spine from the full layout, so lines ran down to boxes not grown yet; the fan now draws the spine only as far as the children shown.
records.problem: In the tree studio, a fan's children are laid out from the start and hidden with opacity. Each child's elbow carried its own stretch of the spine, so the first child shown drew a line toward siblings that were still invisible, and on the owner's phone the half-grown tree had lines running into empty space.
records.approach: While any child of a fan is hidden, the elbows leave out their spine stretch and the fan draws one spine from the parent's line to the children shown, with the litSpine() helper the tap highlight already used. The lit (blue) spine and stub only count children already shown.
records.conditions: Expo app, BranchTree.tsx Fan/Elbow/Stub, growth driven by growPlayer hidden ids, 2026-11-14.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/BranchTree.tsx; e2e/app/quran.spec.ts 'the studio grows a tree to its end'
records.implication: When an animation hides parts of a laid-out view with opacity, anything drawn from that layout (spines, overlays, measured lines) must also be gated by what is shown, or it points at the hidden parts.
records.text: The growth studio keeps the whole tree laid out so the camera never jumps, and fades boxes and connectors in by id. The connectors were split per child: every child's elbow drew half the spine toward each neighbour. Hiding a child's connector hid only its own elbow, so a shown child's half still reached into the hidden sibling's place. The lit path had the same shape of bug once the growing ayah lit its path: the blue spine went to children on the path that were not grown yet. Both now read the hidden set. Tried - First fix lit the spine from lit alone → review caught blue lines toward hidden children; gated by shown.

records.title: A tab page cannot swipe back
records.summary: The Quran tools and the search were hidden tab routes with a back arrow, so iPhone's back swipe (a native stack gesture) never existed for them; putting each bar button's pages in a native stack, set right to left, gave the swipe from the right edge with the page before peeking under it.
records.problem: The owner asked for a back gesture. The pages people go back from (trees, compare, prophets, Tuhfa, the search) were tab routes, so a back arrow switched tabs and nothing could follow the finger or show the page underneath. The pages that were in the root stack (ayah, library, a prophet's story, quiz pages) did swipe back, but from the LEFT edge, against the back arrow on the right.
records.approach: app/(tabs)/(quran) and app/(tabs)/(home) are native Stack groups (URLs unchanged, unstable_settings.initialRouteName keeps the hub or home under a tool opened from anywhere). expo-router's LocaleProvider direction="rtl" at the root makes react-native-screens set the stacks' semanticContentAttribute to right to left, so the back swipe starts at the right edge and pages arrive from the left. fullScreenGestureEnabled is false, because on iOS 26 it defaults to the full-content pop that would fight the cards' own sideways swipes; the gesture-handler pans of the cards also leave the right 24 pt to the back swipe (hitSlop). The tab bar reads the open page from useSegments. toTab navigates withAnchor (initialRouteName only anchors a parsed URL, not an in-app navigate into a stack that has not been drawn), each Quran tool is dangerouslySingular so opening it again brings the one copy forward with its intent, home is reached by navigate then dismissAll (only from inside the tabs: from a page over them the pop would close the page just opened), and toTab only closes the root stack when a root page is in front, so a tree's compare goes back to the tree.
records.conditions: expo-router ~58 (its own react-navigation fork), react-native-screens 4.30, iOS in Expo Go; Android keeps its system back. 2026-11-14.
records.evidence: e2e/app/back.spec.ts; mobile/src/lib/stackOptions.ts; react-native-screens ios/RNSScreenStackHeaderConfig.mm applySemanticContentAttributeIfNeededToNavCtrl (applied even with the header hidden).
records.implication: A page that has a back arrow belongs in a stack, not in the tab bar's hidden routes. A style direction: 'rtl' on a View does not reach native navigation; the navigator's locale direction does.
records.text: The direction: 'rtl' style on the root view lays out rows right to left but never reaches UIKit, so the root stack still slid in from the right and swiped back from the left. react-native-screens reads the direction from the stack's header config, which native-stack fills from the navigation locale, and applies it even when the header is hidden. The web export cannot show the gesture; it checks the stacks back arrow one page back, the hub under a deep-linked tool, the Quran button returning to the open tool . The swipe itself needs a phone. Tried - reading the nested stack from the tab bar's state → the js-tabs bar gets a flattened state without the nested routes; useSegments has them - unstable_settings.initialRouteName alone → a tool opened from home before the Quran tab was ever drawn had no hub under it; navigate needs withAnchor - plain navigate to a tool already lower in the stack → a second copy was pushed and the hidden first copy took the intent; one copy per tool dangerouslySingular, the new name of getId fixes it - dismissTo '/' from another tab → did nothing; navigate then dismissAll goes home and drops the search

records.title: A second text may only correct what it can see
records.summary: The King Fahd riwaya texts fixed real slips in the qira'at dump, but they also moved readings their spelling cannot show, so they now correct only a lone riwaya back to Hafs.
records.problem: A reading list (Quranpedia's dump) and whole riwaya texts (King Fahd Complex) disagree at some words; letting the texts overrule the list moved riwayat into the wrong group.
records.approach: The texts move a riwaya only when the dump sets it apart alone, its own reading is not found in its text, and the only reading found there is Hafs's; al-Bazzi and Qunbul are never moved.
records.conditions: Quranpedia qira'at dump 2026-11-07 (20 riwayat, 5,783 word positions); seven King Fahd texts from fawazahmed0/quran-api; comparison by letters and vowels only.
records.evidence: scripts/quran/buildQiraat.ts; scripts/quran/qiraatFarsh.test.ts; src/app/quran/qiraat/data/qiraatData.test.ts
records.implication: Before a second source overrules the first, list what its notation cannot express (here: a small sin over sad, a dot for tashil, a doubled ta), and limit the correction to cases where that cannot matter.
records.text: The dump names who reads each word; the King Fahd texts print what seven riwayat actually read. A first pass let the texts overrule the dump wherever a riwaya's text matched another group's reading better than its own. It fixed real slips, but it also moved Qunbul's سراط the text marks the sin with a small letter over the sad , riwayat with tashil between two hamzas a dot the letter comparison drops and al-Bazzi's doubled ta a mark the texts place differently . Each of those looked like a disagreement only because the second source writes the reading in a way the comparison cannot read. The correction is now narrow: a riwaya the dump sets apart on its own, whose own reading does not occur in its King Fahd text, and whose text reads exactly Hafs's word, goes back to the Hafs group. Every move is listed in the build's review file. Tried - the texts overrule any group → Qunbul, al-Bazzi and the tashil riwayat moved wrongly - a separate check script that only reports → 254 disagreements, almost all spelling, too many to review

records.title: Questions mixed into one quiz can answer each other
records.summary: Each question kind hid its own answer, but a recite question naming «يس ٢٠» gave away a which-surah question on the same ayah, and a party question's key named the surah.
records.problem: Mixing several question kinds in one quiz: each kind picks its ayat on its own and hides its answer, yet another question in the same quiz, or a field nobody draws, can show it.
records.approach: mixQuestions skips a question whose ayat another picked question already asks (questionAyat: a tree's places, a choice question's ayah), with three times the needed candidates drawn so the quiz still fills; the party view replaces the question key with q<index> until the reveal, beside the blanked answer fields.
records.conditions: Which surah, recite the rest and the trees mixed in one quiz (2026-11-13). Recite names the surah; tree feedback labels every ayah with its surah; which-surah keys were SURAH:<surah>:<ayah>.
records.evidence: shared/quiz/choiceKinds.ts mixQuestions, shared/party/rules.ts viewFor, rules.test.ts
records.implication: When a quiz mixes kinds, check what every other question and every sent field reveals about this one's answer, not only what this question shows.

records.title: A fixed-height box makes iOS cram the rest of a text onto its last line
records.summary: Quran text in a fixed-height, overflow-hidden box showed two lines on iPhone, the second holding all the remaining words and clipped mid-word; numberOfLines and a box sized to its content fix it.
records.problem: The home page's continue-reading card showed a slice of the mushaf page in a 124-point box with overflow hidden. On the owner's iPhone it drew two lines, the second starting with a cut-off word, and left empty space below; the web export looked fine.
records.approach: Drop the fixed height and the fade overlay, and give the Text numberOfLines={3} so React Native lays out exactly three lines and ends the last with an ellipsis. On the website, clamp an inner span with -webkit-line-clamp: 3 so the padding of the outer box doesn't show the marks of the fourth line.
records.conditions: Expo SDK app on iOS, Hafs font at 21/40, justified rtl text made of nested Text spans. The box gave the text less height than its lines needed.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/HomeFeed.tsx ContinueReading; src/components/homepage/Homepage.module.css .pageLines
records.implication: Never limit a text's lines by the height of its container on native: use numberOfLines. Web-export screenshots can't show this; reason from how iOS lays out text, or check on the phone.
records.text: Without numberOfLines, iOS lays text out with clipping line breaks inside whatever height the text view gets. When that height is short of the text, the last line that fits takes every remaining word on one line, and the box clips it. With a justified rtl line, what showed was the end of that long line with a word cut at the right edge, and the space for a third line stayed empty. numberOfLines makes React Native wrap by words, stop at the given line, and end it with an ellipsis, and the box then sizes itself to those lines. Tried - Checked the app's web export → three lines and a fade, no clipping; the bug only shows on the phone. - Fix checked in the web export and the site at phone size, light and dark; not yet confirmed on the iPhone when written.

records.title: A card that redraws a feature loses everything the feature does
records.summary: The home feed's tree, recall and pair cards were drawn again from the data, so none of them zoomed, took typing or opened where it should; rebuilt as wrappers around the real components.
records.problem: A new page (the feed-style home, #703) showed existing features as cards and drew each one again: the tree with BranchTree inside a ScrollView with pointer events off, the recall ayah as empty frames, the pair as two plain ayat. Each copy looked right in a screenshot and did nothing the real feature does.
records.approach: Each card now renders the component its page uses. App: the tree card is TreePager (an `embedded` mode that keeps no branches place, has no studio, and lets an unzoomed tree pass vertical drags to the page via TreeCard `inScroll`); the recall card uses the mushaf's WriteBox and Veil with the write logic moved out of Reader into useWriteBoxes (shared/quran/writeAyah.ts typeInBox, gradeWritten); the pair card is CompareCard with an `onOpen` button. Website: BranchTree with zoom and a `steppable.onStep` callback, the read page's WriteBox and a useWriteBoxes hook moved out of ReaderView, the compare page's Card with a `page` prop. The branches tab's endless loading came from change() setting the same list object again, so the list effect also depends on `start`.
records.conditions: Expo app (RN gesture handler pan inside a vertical ScrollView) and Next.js site, 2026-11-13. Owner report: the tree card drew wrong, could not switch, zoom or scroll, and opened an endless spinner; the recall boxes took no input.
records.evidence: mobile/src/components/HomeFeed.tsx, mobile/src/lib/useWriteBoxes.tsx, src/components/homepage/HomeFeed.tsx, src/app/quran/read/useWriteBoxes.tsx; e2e/app/home.spec.ts and e2e/web/pages.spec.ts tests per card
records.implication: A card, preview or widget that shows an existing feature renders that feature's component, adding props for the new place (embedded, onOpen, page) instead of drawing it again. Before building one, find the component the feature's own page uses. Each such card gets a UI test that uses it (zoom or swipe, typing, the tap that opens its page), not a screenshot.
records.text: The home feed was built as a social-style page with its own post cards. Each post took the feature's data and drew it again: the tree card put BranchTree in a sideways ScrollView , wrapped it in a Pressable and turned its pointer events off, so it could not zoom, pan, light a path or switch trees, and the press fought the page's scroll. The recall card drew a frame per hidden word with no field behind it. The pair card drew both ayat as text. All three passed review and screenshots, because a screenshot only shows how a card looks, not what it does. The fix was to delete the copies and render the real components. Each component needed a small prop for its new place. The branches pager must not overwrite the tab's saved place or claim its studio, and on the home page an unzoomed tree must leave vertical drags to the page. The reader's write mode kept its typing rules inline, so they moved into a hook that the reader and the card both call. Opening a tree also hit a separate bug. change on the branches tab blanks the list and then sets the list again. When the new list was the same object the shared empty list , the effect that rebuilds the trees did not run, and the tab showed the spinner forever. Anything that opened a tree into the default list could hit it. Tried - Fix each card's symptom a pan here, an input there → stopped by the owner: every symptom came from the cards being copies.

records.title: A pair must be named in the quoted sentence, not the one next to it
records.summary: Ayah pairs shown under a book quote came from sentences around the quote, so the page showed links the quote did not make.
records.problem: A book passage on why one surah follows another names ayat in several sentences. We quoted one sentence and showed ayah pairs taken from the others, so the card's quote did not support its pairs.
records.approach: Check every pair against the displayed quote only. Widen the quote with «…» cuts until it names both ayat, or drop the pair. Match every quote to its cited page in the turath.io text of the book, fuzzily only where an obvious typo of the digital text was corrected.
records.conditions: /quran/order: 74 aims from al-Biqa'i and 73 links from al-Suyuti and Ibn al-Zubayr, from Shamela books 9098, 1404, 9992 and 1388. The review found 10 links whose pairs were named outside the quote.
records.evidence: Namaq PR for /quran/order (commits 1bcae6d and 5fc5977); shared/quran/surahOrder.ts; docs/plans/quran-order-sources.md.
records.implication: When a citation carries derived items (pairs, chips, colours), check each item against the exact text shown, not against the page or passage it came from.
records.text: Al-Suyuti often makes a link in three steps: it names an ayah at the end of one surah, names another at the start of the next, then concludes in a short sentence. The short conclusion read best on a card, so we quoted it and showed the ayat from the earlier sentences. An independent review against the book's pages found that the pairs on 10 of the 73 links were not in the quoted words. The fix keeps the earlier sentences, with «…» marking each cut, so the reader sees the book name both ayat. The quotes were also checked by script against their cited pages: the text was normalized diacritics, hamza forms and inline references removed , and fuzzy matching was used only for corrected typos such as «الحدسيد» to «الحديد». Tried - Quoting the concluding sentence and taking the pairs from the same page → the quotes were accurate, but the pairs were not supported by them.

records.title: Filtered identities need the original selection
records.summary: Autocomplete hashed filtered passages that the full-corpus resolver could not find.
records.problem: A filtered list creates identifiers from reduced membership while its detail resolver identifies the original full selection.
records.approach: Assign comparison IDs before filtering, keep legacy aliases, and share the same scoped inventory between browsing and autocomplete.
records.conditions: Quran trees over 6,236 ayat; review found 232 of 298 range-generated suggestion IDs absent from the full resolver.
records.evidence: Namaq PR #524 at c63417e1 and PR #525 at 6896a5db; regression tests and independent audit.
records.implication: All juz-one word-tree suggestion IDs resolve against the full-corpus inventory; scoped search and saved-only results obey the same eligibility filters.
records.text: The page resolved tree IDs against the full corpus, but autocomplete rebuilt phrase trees inside the juz range and hashed their reduced membership. Independent review reproduced 232 unresolved IDs among 298 juz-one candidates. The shared inventory now assigns the ID from the original word selections, then prunes occurrences for the current scope. The displayed shared phrase can expand after filtering without changing the comparison identity. Saved-only browsing also intersects the eligible inventory; a direct old bookmark URL remains a separate compatibility path. Evidence comes from Namaq PR 524 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/524 and PR 525 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/525 . src/lib/quran/branchInventory.ts owns scoped inventory eligibility; src/lib/quran/mutashabih/evidence.ts scopes citations; src/app/quran/compare/CompareView.test.tsx independently checks rendered passage coverage. The implication is to check the final visible selection, including its evidence, identity and initially displayed text, after every scope transformation.

records.title: A citation does not authorize every chip
records.summary: A valid source comparison still carried an incorrect singular/plural label and spread chips to uncited members.
records.problem: A container has a source citation, so its generated labels are treated as supported for every member and every filtered view.
records.approach: Retain exact source selections, scope citations first, and derive published chips, examples and connectors only from surviving evidence.
records.conditions: Thirty recorded book cases across seventeen cited comparison groups in a 1,141-group inventory; both خطاياكم and خطيئاتكم are plural.
records.evidence: Namaq PR #524 at c63417e1 and PR #525 at 6896a5db; regression tests and independent audit.
records.implication: Uncited gender chips are hidden; the incorrect number tag for two plural forms is removed; filtering out the source comparison removes its chips and book-only eligibility.
records.text: The خطاياكم / خطيئاتكم comparison had book evidence but was labelled جمع وإفراد. Source support for comparing the words did not support that label: both forms are plural. The tag was removed. Another group carried a citation for 2:129 and 2:151 plus uncited members 3:164 and 62:2. Filtering to those latter members previously hid the citation while leaving its chip and example. Evidence now carries the exact selections and is scoped before chips, connectors or the book-only filter are computed. Evidence comes from Namaq PR 524 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/524 and PR 525 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/525 . src/lib/quran/branchInventory.ts owns scoped inventory eligibility; src/lib/quran/mutashabih/evidence.ts scopes citations; src/app/quran/compare/CompareView.test.tsx independently checks rendered passage coverage. The implication is to check the final visible selection, including its evidence, identity and initially displayed text, after every scope transformation.

records.title: Rendered context needs coverage checks
records.summary: Every selected ayah existed in computed rows, but most were initially hidden in one curated comparison.
records.problem: A comparison reports complete selected coverage while its renderer collapses the unmatched parts by default.
records.approach: Reuse the existing passage renderer, open unmatched context for curated selections, and derive expected verse coverage independently from the Quran text.
records.conditions: The Salih comparison selects 7:73-79 and 26:141-159; previously only one of nineteen ayat on the second side was visible initially.
records.evidence: Namaq PR #524 at c63417e1 and PR #525 at 6896a5db; regression tests and independent audit.
records.implication: Tests verify all seven curated selections are initially visible with original verse numbers and without duplicates; explicit custom comparisons retain their previous collapsed context.
records.text: The existing matcher already retained every selected ayah in either a matched block or an unmatched context row. That did not make the complete passage visible. Its context rows started collapsed, so the Salih selection initially exposed only one of nineteen ayat on the second side. Curated mode now opens the context and reuses the same renderer. Tests derive each expected ayah and reference from the corpus rather than trusting the aligner row counts. The interface calls the algorithmic links lexical matches because shared words can connect different narrative moments. Evidence comes from Namaq PR 524 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/524 and PR 525 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/525 . src/lib/quran/branchInventory.ts owns scoped inventory eligibility; src/lib/quran/mutashabih/evidence.ts scopes citations; src/app/quran/compare/CompareView.test.tsx independently checks rendered passage coverage. The implication is to check the final visible selection, including its evidence, identity and initially displayed text, after every scope transformation.

records.title: Shared forms do not pair repeated word occurrences
records.summary: A repeated ما inherited another occurrence's exact match, while similarity-search keys omitted the preposition needed for مِنْ and مِنْهَا.
records.problem: Text comparison reuses matches between repeated occurrences and treats a search index's omitted tokens as absent evidence.
records.approach: Keep the existing LCS occurrence selection, compare corresponding selected occurrences, and reuse complete stem roots and lemmas. Apply the same matcher to tree segments without crossing ayah boundaries.
records.conditions: Quran branch comparison over 6,236 ayat and 5,174 multi-ayah tree groups, using corpus morphology and original reader words.
records.evidence: Namaq PR #512; regressions for 2:35/7:19, 2:170/31:21, tree offsets and default-view navigation; 3,502 tests, lint, typecheck and build passed.
records.implication: Select concrete occurrences before classifying their forms, and check whether an index intentionally drops information before using it as comparison evidence.
records.text: In 2:170 and 31:21, the first ما pair agreed, but the second pair differed in its marks. The matcher collected every form under the shared key and used that collection to classify each occurrence. The first pair's shared form therefore made the second occurrence in 2:170 look exact. Selecting concrete occurrences and comparing their corresponding forms made the second pair purple on both sides. The other report crossed a different boundary. The similarity-search keys intentionally omitted prepositions and classified حيث differently by part of speech. Full STEM metadata was already available in the tree inventory. Reusing it paired مِنْ with مِنْهَا by lemma and recognized حَيْثُ as exact. The legend now says “Same lemma or root.” Independent review also found that a subtree link dropped an explicit tree override above a saved matrix default. A page regression followed the generated link before the fix, then verified that the destination stayed a tree. The second review found no further defects. Evidence is Namaq PR 512 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/512 , src/lib/quran/ayahContext.test.ts and src/app/quran/branches/page.test.tsx. The full inventory test checks equal exact and lemma/root counts and disjoint, in-range marks. All 3,502 tests passed with two workers; the production build, lint and TypeScript checks passed too. The implication is to distinguish a search index's selection policy from a comparison's evidence needs. An exact match belongs to a tuple of occurrences, not to a word key's collection of possible forms.

records.title: A pairwise match can change after cropping
records.summary: Candidate pairs passed the matching policy, but selecting shorter spans required checking those exact spans again.
records.problem: A group passes a pairwise predicate before its inputs are transformed, then publishes transformed members without repeating the predicate.
records.approach: Build groups whose every pair matches, select the word spans, then compare every selected pair again. Retain valid groups and recover qualifying pairs when a larger cropped group fails. Rank closeness using the original complete ayat.
records.conditions: Quran comparisons over 6,236 ayat, with local spans, morphology-aware matching, retained book cases and tree/matrix views.
records.evidence: Namaq PR #514, source commit 0daf6adeb6908032a3212987293853c73661aa0b; engine.ts final clipped-span validation and wholePlace coverage, engine.test.ts automatic-pair and ranking regressions.
records.implication: Recheck an invariant after the transformation that produces the published inputs, and define the denominator of a user-facing similarity score.
records.text: The new comparison inventory first compared complete ayat and built groups whose members all matched one another. It then chose shorter word spans for the card. Those choices can remove different parts of different ayat, so the earlier pairwise result does not establish that the displayed spans still meet the same policy. The builder now checks every cropped pair and falls back to qualifying pairs when a larger group loses that property. Review found a related denominator error. A short shared phrase could score one when measured against itself, putting it ahead of nearly identical complete ayat in “closest first.” The final score uses whole-ayah coverage across every pair. The 2:4/4:162 group scores about 0.346, while 2:48/2:123 scores about 0.895. The selected spans still decide what to compare and highlight. Evidence comes from Namaq PR 514 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/514 , src/lib/quran/mutashabih/engine.ts and src/lib/quran/mutashabih/engine.test.ts at commit 0daf6adeb6908032a3212987293853c73661aa0b. Tests cover the final published word spans and compare a short shared phrase against a near-complete parallel. The invariant belongs to the final representation. Ranking also needs its own measure when the UI asks how much of a complete item agrees.

records.title: A filter draft must outlive its pending URL
records.summary: Rapid filter changes lost a picked value, and a partial fix restored a cleared value from the old address.
records.problem: A second live filter change is computed from URL state that has not caught up with the first change.
records.approach: Keep the latest complete draft in a ref, reconcile only matching navigation responses, restore it on browser history changes, and replace all managed URL filter keys from that draft.
records.conditions: Next.js server-rendered Quran browse results with live multi-select surah and juz filters, React client controls and delayed router replacement.
records.evidence: Namaq PR #514, source commit 0daf6adeb6908032a3212987293853c73661aa0b; GroupFilters.tsx and GroupFilters.test.tsx; Playwright multi-select navigation check.
records.implication: Race tests should leave router.replace pending while another input changes, including a deletion followed by an addition.
records.text: Picking a second surah before the first route finished could lose the first pick. The optimistic state reverted before the server returned the updated filter props. A ref holding the latest complete draft kept both selections, and an older response was ignored until the returned filters matched that draft. Browser history changes deliberately restore the draft from the new address. The next review found the reverse failure. Starting with a word-order filter, clearing it and immediately enabling book-only results could restore the cleared filter. The second request began with the old address and replaced only its own key. The fix deletes every managed filter key, then serializes the latest draft. Other URL state, such as the selected view and current group, stays available. Evidence comes from Namaq PR 514 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/514 , src/app/quran/branches/GroupFilters.tsx and src/app/quran/branches/GroupFilters.test.tsx at commit 0daf6adeb6908032a3212987293853c73661aa0b. The regression leaves the mocked address unchanged between clearing one filter and adding another. The browser check also picks multiple surahs and a juz while navigation remains asynchronous. A complete draft needs complete serialization. Updating only the key of the latest click lets old keys survive in the address.

records.title: Absorbing a phrase must preserve its entry points
records.summary: Combining overlapping Quran trees fixed duplicate diagrams but needed separate checks for autocomplete, zoom targets, and answer offsets.
records.problem: Combining overlapping text groups removes entry points that search and navigation still need.
records.approach: Retain larger overlapping occurrence groups first, keep absorbed wording as search aliases, and use the underlying phrase inventory for focused links and zoom discovery. Keep conjunctions attached to whole words and move answer offsets with the trunk boundary.
records.conditions: Arabic Quran branch trees generated from 6,236 ayat, with shared phrases identified by word offsets and morphology.
records.evidence: namaq PR #473; page, phraseTrees, branch-phrases route, and branchQuestions regression tests; 3,289 tests passed.
records.implication: When combining groups, test each way a user reaches the absorbed group and each consumer of its word offsets.
records.text: The branch page showed the wording shared by 43:83 and 70:42 separately from an overlapping tree that included 52:45. It also put an attached ف in its own node. A three-ayah fixture caught the duplicate and the detached letter. The actual juz 25–30 page then exposed another overlap: الذي يوعدون and يومهم الذي share a word without either anchor containing the other. Retaining larger groups first and absorbing a smaller group only where every occurrence overlaps a retained anchor produced one tree for the reported passages. That changed more than the list. Independent review found that submitted search and the suggestion API had aliases, but local autocomplete did not. It also found that absorbed phrases could still open by URL while their zoom buttons had vanished. Page tests reproduced both failures before the fixes. Moving a whole first-word variant before the trunk also changed the answer offset used by the quiz, so a separate regression checks where its answers begin. Evidence comes from Namaq PR 473 https://github.com/msskzx/namaq/pull/473 , src/app/quran/branches/page.test.tsx, src/lib/quran/phraseTrees.test.ts, and src/lib/quiz/branchQuestions.test.ts. The regenerated inventory matched its builder, the underlying ayah data stayed unchanged, and all 3,289 tests passed. Combining groups needs checks for typing a query, submitting it, opening an old link, discovering a focused view, and consuming the resulting offsets. A correct diagram alone does not establish that those entry points still work.

records.title: A tree answer must preserve the path, including where a text ends
records.summary: Completing every branch node requires whole-subtree matching and citations on internal nodes as well as leaves.
records.problem: A free-text quiz must ask for every node of a compressed text tree while accepting reordered answers without detaching children from their parents.
records.approach: Reused the explorer tree with custom non-root fields, required every node's complete words, paired whole subtrees by shape, and retained each node's ending-text references in feedback.
records.conditions: Shared-opening questions derived from Quran ayat; pieces contain at most six ayat; one ayah may end at a node that also has children.
records.evidence: src/lib/quiz/branchAnswers.ts; src/app/quizzes/BranchAnswers.tsx; src/lib/quiz/branchQuestions.test.ts
records.implication: Test completion and feedback against a real tree containing an internal terminal node, not only synthetic trees whose texts all end at leaves.
records.text: The shared-opening quiz previously asked for the first split. Asking for the whole tree changes what an answer means: every non-root node needs all its words, and sibling reordering must move a parent together with its descendants. The implementation reuses the explorer's renderer and pairs subtrees only when their shapes agree, choosing the pairing with the most correct nodes. The real يطوف عليهم tree exposes a quieter constraint. Of its three non-root nodes, ولدان مخلدون ends 56:17 and also has a child continuing 76:19. A leaf-only citation pass would lose 56:17 even though the tree still looked complete. Feedback keeps the references held by every node. Evidence: src/lib/quran/branches.ts keeps ending ayat separately from children; src/lib/quiz/branchAnswers.ts pairs subtrees; src/app/quizzes/BranchAnswers.tsx renders each matched node's references. The real-tree assertion lives in src/lib/quiz/branchQuestions.test.ts. Implications: test a real tree whose internal node also ends a text. Checking only leaf count or a flat bag of answer strings cannot prove that paths and references survived.

records.title: Leaving mdx out of pageExtensions broke only the dev server
records.summary: The production build passed while every lesson page in dev failed with an error about React internals.
records.problem: A Next.js dev server fails on MDX pages with a React internals error while the production build passes.
records.approach: Set pageExtensions to only ts and tsx so MDX files outside app/ would not become routes; found the dev build compiled .mdx against userland React because Next's alias condition is built from pageExtensions. Adding mdx to pageExtensions held.
records.conditions: Next.js App Router site with MDX content under content/ outside app/, pageExtensions set in next.config.ts.
records.evidence: Fix in next.config.ts (pageExtensions: ["ts", "tsx", "mdx"]); alias rules in node_modules/next/dist/build/create-compiler-aliases.js
records.implication: When a change touches next.config.ts, open one page of each kind in the dev server before calling it done.
records.text: Lessons live under content/ , outside app/ , so pageExtensions was set to "ts", "tsx" to keep MDX files from becoming routes by accident. next build passed and rendered every page. next dev failed on every lesson with Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'recentlyCreatedOwnerStacks' , an error from React's development JSX runtime that says nothing about MDX or configuration. The compiled lesson chunk imported node_modules/react/jsx-dev-runtime.js , the userland React, while the page around it ran on the React that Next vendors. Next aliases react/jsx-runtime to its own copy only for files that match its code condition, and that condition is built from pageExtensions . An .mdx file outside the list was compiled but never aliased. Production uses the plain JSX runtime, which does not touch the field, so only development broke. Evidence: .next/server/_rsc_content_lessons_..._index_mdx.js importing rsc /./node_modules/react/jsx-runtime.js ; the alias rules in node_modules/next/dist/build/create-compiler-aliases.js ; the fix in next.config.ts pageExtensions: "ts", "tsx", "mdx" . Implications: a green next build does not show that next dev works. When a change touches next.config.ts , open one page of each kind in the dev server before calling it done. An error from deep inside React that mentions internals usually means two copies of React met, so check which react each chunk imports before reading the stack.

records.title: The coordinator deleted the folder a subagent was converting
records.summary: While four subagents converted lessons, the coordinator committed the deletion of the folder one of them was reading from.
records.problem: A coordinator agent changed or deleted files that a running subagent was told to read.
records.approach: Four subagents converted lessons in parallel while the coordinator ran git rm -r on the folder they read from. One subagent recovered the sources from the earlier commit with git archive and finished.
records.conditions: Four parallel subagents converting namaq lessons to MDX from one live checkout while the coordinator edited the same checkout.
records.evidence: namaq commit 773a035d removing docs/lessons/; subagent report of reading from git archive 607669f6
records.implication: Hand a subagent a snapshot (a commit hash or a scratchpad copy), and do not delete or move anything a running subagent was told to read.
records.text: Four subagents converted namaq's lessons to MDX in parallel, each told to read the old HTML from namaq's docs/lessons/ . While they ran, the coordinator moved on to the namaq half of the move and ran git rm -r docs/lessons in the same checkout. One subagent found its sources gone halfway through lesson 0001. It recovered them from the commit before the deletion with git archive and finished, and the text-parity check later showed nothing lost. A less careful agent would have reported "files not found" or, worse, converted from memory. Evidence: namaq commit 773a035d removing docs/lessons/ , made while the text-to-evidence conversion was still running; that subagent's report of reading from git archive 607669f6 . Implications: a delegated task's inputs are frozen until it reports back. Hand a subagent a snapshot a commit hash, or a copy in the scratchpad , not a live path in a checkout someone else is editing, and do not delete or move anything a running subagent was told to read.

records.title: Date.parse accepted the thirtieth of February
records.summary: A date check built on Date.parse let 2026-02-30 through, and its test could not notice because it only tried a month that does not exist.
records.problem: Validating that a YYYY-MM-DD string is a real calendar date in JavaScript.
records.approach: Checked the pattern and that Date.parse did not return NaN; review showed V8 rolls 2026-02-30 over to March 2, so the check now round-trips the date through toISOString and compares.
records.conditions: Node 22 and Bun on V8/JavaScriptCore; dates written as plain YYYY-MM-DD strings in record metadata.
records.evidence: distillate PR #4, first review cycle; lib/records.ts checkRecord
records.implication: Test a date validator with a day that overflows its month (2026-02-30, 2026-04-31), not only with an impossible month.
records.text: The record schema requires a date in YYYY-MM-DD form. The first check matched the pattern and called Date.parse , treating NaN as invalid. The test for "not a real calendar date" used 2026-13-45 , which every parser rejects, so it passed. The reviewer tried 2026-02-30 . Date.parse returned a timestamp for March 2: the engine rolls an overflowing day into the next month instead of refusing it. Any record could have claimed a day that never happened. The fix parses the string as UTC midnight and requires toISOString .slice 0, 10 to give back the same string. A rolled-over date comes back different and fails. Evidence: lib/records.ts checkRecord , and the tests for 2026-02-30 and 2026-04-31 in lib/records.test.ts. Implications: a date check is only as good as the cases it is shown to reject. Include a day that overflows its month, since that is the case lenient parsers accept.

records.title: The fix for a stale search box wiped what the reader was typing
records.summary: Resyncing a search box from the URL treated the URL's own lag as an outside change and reset the box mid-typing.
records.problem: Keeping a text input that writes to the URL in step with the URL when the URL also changes from outside, such as back navigation or a link.
records.approach: First reset the box whenever the URL's q differed from the last value written, which wiped text while router.replace lagged behind typing; now the component remembers the values it wrote and resets only for a value it never wrote.
records.conditions: Next.js 15 App Router client component using useSearchParams and router.replace, where the URL updates after the input's own state.
records.evidence: distillate PR #5; components/records/RecordSearch.tsx and its tests
records.implication: A component that writes to the URL must tell its own pending writes apart from outside navigation; test it with a URL that arrives one keystroke behind.
records.text: The records search box keeps its text in React state and writes it to the URL as q . Review found that the box kept "highlight" after the reader followed a link to /records , because the state was read from the URL only on mount. The first fix compared the URL's q on every render with the last value the component had written, and reset the box when they differed. Writing the regression test showed what that did while typing: router.replace lands after the input's own re-render, so for a moment the URL still holds the previous text, which differs from what was just written, and the box was reset to it. A fast typist would have watched letters vanish. The fix that held keeps a short list of values the component wrote. When the URL's q changes to one of them, it is the component's own write arriving late and is ignored. Any other value came from outside, so the box takes it. The check only reads the list and clears it, so running it twice in one render changes nothing. Evidence: components/records/RecordSearch.tsx; the tests "keeps the latest typed text when the URL arrives one keystroke behind" and "clears the search box when the URL loses its query after mount" in components/records/RecordSearch.test.tsx. Implications: two-way sync between an input and the URL needs to know which changes are its own. Test it with the URL lagging, not only with the URL updating at once.

records.title: A mock router too fast to show the race it was meant to catch
records.summary: A regression test for a URL race passed on the broken code, because the mocked router updated the URL instantly.
records.problem: A test of a timing bug passes on the code it is meant to catch, because the test double removes the timing.
records.approach: Ran the new test against the code before the fix, saw it pass, and made the mocked router.replace skip the URL update for the typing step so the URL lags as in the browser; the test then failed on the old code and passed on the fix.
records.conditions: Vitest with jsdom, next/navigation mocked so that router.replace sets the search string synchronously.
records.evidence: distillate PR #5; the test "keeps the typed text when a filter changes before the URL catches up"
records.implication: Run every regression test against the code before the fix and watch it fail; when a race is involved, make the double reproduce the delay.
records.text: Review reported that changing a filter right after typing could drop the typed text from the URL. The test written for it typed, changed a filter, and checked the URL. It passed on the fixed code, and it also passed on the old code. The mock for next/navigation updated the search string inside router.replace , so the next render already saw the new URL. In the browser, replace lands later, which is the whole bug. The mock had removed the delay the test was about. Making the mocked replace skip the update for the typing step put the delay back. The test then failed on the old code, passed on the fix, and in passing exposed a second bug in the first fix see the record that builds on this one . Evidence: components/records/RecordSearch.test.tsx, where the test calls nav.replace.mockImplementationOnce = {} before typing. Implications: a test that has not been seen to fail on the old code has not been shown to test anything. For timing bugs, the double has to keep the timing.

records.title: A trailing slash in .gitignore let a node_modules symlink into the commit
records.summary: node_modules/ in .gitignore matches only directories, so a worktree's node_modules symlink was committed.
records.problem: A symlinked node_modules in a git worktree is committed even though .gitignore lists node_modules/.
records.approach: Spotted the symlink in the staged files after commit, removed it from the index and changed the ignore rule to node_modules without the slash, which matches files and symlinks too.
records.conditions: Git worktree whose node_modules is a symlink to the main checkout's, staged with git add -A.
records.evidence: distillate PR #4; .gitignore
records.implication: Ignore node_modules without a trailing slash in repositories whose worktrees symlink it, and read git status before committing with git add -A.
records.text: Worktrees here share the main checkout's packages through a symlink: each worktree's node_modules points at the main checkout's. The repository ignored node_modules/ . In git's ignore syntax a trailing slash means "directories only", and a symlink is a file, so git add -A staged it. The commit summary listed A node_modules . The fix was git rm --cached node_modules and an ignore rule without the slash, which matches a file, a symlink or a directory of that name. Evidence: .gitignore. Implications: where worktrees symlink shared folders, ignore them without the trailing slash, and look at what git add -A staged before committing.

records.title: Arabic inside English prose has no element to style, so the font itself had to be larger
records.summary: Inline Arabic in MDX paragraphs carries no markup, so setting it larger than the English needed size-adjust on a self-hosted Arabic face.
records.problem: Setting Arabic words larger than the English around them when they sit inline in prose with no element, class or lang attribute to target.
records.approach: Put the Arabic face after the English serif in one font stack so Arabic glyphs fall back to it, and self-hosted its Arabic subset through next/font/local with a size-adjust declaration, since next/font/google takes no declarations.
records.conditions: Next.js 15 next/font; MDX lessons may not carry class, className or style; Amiri's Arabic subset from Google Fonts; inline Arabic in lessons such as text-to-evidence 0006.
